You can say society owes you a living. But you cannot say that society owes you elite status. 

A lot of people who took their high social status for granted feel that it's a God-given right. But it's not.


Corey (@CoreyLeander)

Of course not! Why would you think me criticizing your plan to pacify us with uniform UBI is evidence I feel I should be paid more than a waiter? 

But paying everyone the same UBI is zombified dystopia. Sounds like uniform communism to me.



— https://nitter.net/Core

Anti-immigration people continuously scream that "Immigration reduces wages!".

But it doesn't. Trump's ICE raids aren't raising wages for American workers. If anything, they're HURTING wages, especially for the American working class.

noahpinion.blog/p/roundup-82…

"God made men differ in intelligence, but Sam Altman made them equal" is a line I'm going to be using a lot


tomie (@tomieinlove)

The prostitute comment is quite apt. God made men differ in strength, but Sam Colt made them equal. Likewise, God made men differ in intelligence, but Sam Altman made them equal. We’re now competing on beauty. The concern is not if scaling has hit a wall. It’s if you have.



— https://nitter.net/tomieinlove/status/2057256093336945139#m

I'm not sure this is a great idea, given the obvious potential for medical knowledge to be used to kill all humans.


Lost Nomad (@lost_nomad__)

The field of mathematics is going to get solved by AI largely because the training data is comprehensive and publicly available

Which is why it’s of utmost importance that we start relaxing privacy regulations and feeding it tons of medical data AS SOON AS POSSIBLE



— https://nitter.net/lost_nomad__/status/2057262969751265721#m

I would like to see a model of the number of interesting problems that shows that it's infinite!


Daniel Litt (@littmath)

Unit distances result is very exciting, but re: “math is solved” — humans regularly solve long-open problems, and yet infinitely more interesting open problems remain.



— https://nitter.net/littmath/status/2057288190902333727#m
Why do you think you deserve to be paid more than a cashier or a waiter?

The slow nationalization of U.S. industry continues


Andrew Curran (@AndrewCurran_)

The White House is awarding $2 billion in grants - $1 billion of it directly to IBM - to nine quantum computing companies and taking a equity stake in all of them.  A quantum industry executive order is also being drafted.





— https://nitter.net/AndrewCurran_/status/2057421528829186077#m
I mean, I've been writing for literally 15 years about how tons of economists are just spinning their wheels making theories no one ever believes or applies. And that was before AI.

Zero downside that I can see. That would be great. The economy does not exist in order to be a jobs program for economists.


Corey (@CoreyLeander)

What a fucking asshole lmao

“What’s the downside of AI discovering all possible economic models, all their mathematical results, & completely analyzing all existing economic data against every such possible economic model over every possible time horizon?”



— https://nitter.net/CoreyLeander/status/2057339671659594193#m

Did you see this post I wrote?

noahpinion.blog/p/superintel…

The reason Boomers give good dating advice is that although a few things have changed, the basics have not. Guys who use "the apps" as an excuse to screech online instead of getting out there and actually dating people are NOT the guys you should be listening to.


Westside L.A. Guy (@WestsideLAGuy)

Boomers’ dating advice is comically outdated & should be ignored. Like asking a 1970 Harvard graduate for admissions advice.

The men who give actual good advice:

-Competed in the modern dating

Crime is down in America, but corruption is way up. 

noahpinion.blog/p/roundup-82…

Well, clicking on blog posts and reading them instead of just responding to tweets, for one.

I find this to be an almost impossible task for the vast majority of humans


Dylan Higbie (@DuvalEaton)

If AI eventually dominates all aspects of human achievement what is left for humans to try and strive to achieve?



— https://nitter.net/DuvalEaton/status/2057326650514129176#m
What's the downside of AI discovering all the math that can possibly be discovered? Math doesn't exist as a jobs program for IMO gold medalists.
Is that time of year when much of my diet consists of the end-of-the-year “banquets” that my kids’ various extracurricular activities throw for them.

A legend, a pioneer, and smarter and funnier than 95% of anyone to ever hold elected office. 

www.huffpost.com/entry/barney...

I feel like I became aware of Applebee’s, Chili’s, and TGI Fridays, pretty much exactly the same time in the mid 1990s. It’s looking likely that Applebee’s will be the last one standing, and I would not have guessed that.

Yes. Words that are not palindromes but they appear in a very well known palindrome sentence. That’s not hard to grasp. 

And it’s okay that you haven’t ever heard or read “Able was I ere I saw Elba.” So this is a chance to learn, not a chance to whine that other people know something you don’t.

WAITRESS: Welcome to I Love The 90s Grill and Bar! What can I getcha?
KID: I want the Macarena And Cheese!
WAITRESS: For you, ma’am?
MOM: The…Rodney King Crab?
WAITRESS: And you, sir?
DAD: The eggs.
WAITRESS: You have to say it.
DAD: *sigh* Jesus Christ. Okay. I’ll take the Sarajevos Rancheros

(That joke would work so much better if you hadn’t already used the word hog in the original Skeet — but I really can’t get upset that your post — which was not intended to be a set up for me — doesn’t work as well as as a set up for me as I would like it to)
That was created by Hog Hefner, right?
My wife’s Norwegian family love the joke “what’s one thing Sweden has that Norway doesn’t? Nice neighbors,” to which our Swedish friends say “yes, the Finns are lovely.”
It is sad. Up until now the Swedish Chef has been such an accurate depiction of Swedish culture and cuisine …

They’re opening a Swedish chef themed restaurant at Disney World. While this is welcome and long overdue, I hope there is at least some chance that my food could come to life and attack me. Otherwise, what’s the point?

www.disneytouristblog.com/new-muppets-...
One must imagine Sisyphus getting to the fireworks factory.

“Hi, Roma people. We’re really sorry that we called you that word for so long. Honestly, most of us didn’t know it was a slur. We thought it was kind of cool sounding! … no … I know. That doesn’t make it okay. It’s just … there’s this musical … it’s kind of one of the best ones …”
My 10-year-old on dinosaur chicken nuggets: They’re the best. Even if you don’t like dinos, you can just cut off the head, feet, and tails.  And then it’s like you defeated the dinosaurs.

Among the many things I find fascinating about this list is the fact that whoever assembled it put it in alphabetical order except for the last two, because apparently they thought it would be better to end with Wicked Alice rather than Wide-ass Nellie.
It’s weird, watching the Daredevil show and seeing Kingpin murder people with his bare hands and set heavily-armed maniacs against civilians, and knowing he’s still a better human being than Trump. ￼

Hey, Universe!

STOP KILLING THE WRONG OLD MEN! 

www.huffpost.com/entry/ted-tu...

Leslie Bibb is awesome and I would never want to body shame anybody, or question the choices they make for their own bodies, especially knowing the pressure that actresses feel to stay thin. But this is more carbohydrates than this woman has eaten since the Obama administration.
If I were a celebrity I would live in constant fear that I might get invited to the Met Gala.
Luke Skywalker is the ultimate Generation X icon because, like so many of us, he learned everything he needed to know from a Muppet.
Roundup #82: Staring in wonder at the world. Crime; ICE raids; AI hate; Oligarchy; AI math; Small businesses; Neoliberal Claude; Slacker AGI; The Technium
All non-drone militaries are obsolete
Dating advice for men. Don't believe the incel stuff. Romance is very possible for regular, average men.
Yes, Europeans are poorer than Americans. Comfortable, leisurely, pleasant stagnation is just not good enough for the modern age.
Trump actually started to decouple America from China. The "economic divorce" between the two countries is proceeding slowly, but it is proceeding.
Tyrants are losing wars. Ruthlessness and machismo will only get you so far in a technological world.
Do billionaires earn their money?
Barack Obama was a successful President
Could development economics be more useful?
AI's big messaging pivot. Some top AI leaders now say their technology will create jobs. Should we believe them?
California's "billionaire tax" is the wrong approach. Left-populist instincts are leading to silly policy ideas.
Roundup #81: Back to our regular programming. National debt; AI cyberattacks; Phone bans; AI and coding jobs; Millennials vs. Boomers; Public order; California YIMBYism
Scoring the Jensen-Dwarkesh debate. Export controls are holding back Chinese AI. Should we keep them?
The moderately easy problem of consciousness. Before deciding if computers are self-aware, let's figure out how humans become self-aware.
Why shoplifting is bad. It may feel like a small act of rebellion, but it hurts a lot of people who don't deserve it.
